findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One staff member on site was observed to have an expired certification (CFPM certificate, but no Food Handler’s certificate in supplementation). All staff who do any degree of food handling must have a minimum of a Food Handler certificate, to be obtained within 30 days of hire and maintained every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be no sealant connecting the newly refinished door frame to the wall in the cold room. Ensure this area is sealed to prevent moisture from entering the walls.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed the facility did not have signed employee health reporting forms. The inspector provided blank copies. All present employees signed the forms and the rest will sign when they report to work. Ensure the signed copies remain at the facility.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed the PIC’s allergen awareness training is expired. No one else at the facility has their allergen awareness training. The PIC stated they will take the test again promptly. Ensure that certified sanitation managers obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The clear door cooler in the front of the facility holds mostly drinks, but does have some horseradish and pickled items.  The horseradish had a temperature of 47F (probed).  All horseradish was pulled and discarded.  Ensure cooler temperatures containing foods are monitored to prevent contamination.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: Ensure all CFMs at facility have completed online Allergen Awareness training by next routine inspection. Information provided at time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  The following products were observed out of temperature in the customer reach-in cooler as a result of temp abuse in defrosting cycle: chicken salad (47), ground italian sausage (51), ground beef (46). Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Out-of-temperature food was discarded by CFM. Throughout course of inspection, CFM lowered temperature and inspectors periodically checked fridge products to ensure temperature was decreasing.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Observed cardboard being used in the reach-in freezer and under prep table as storage containers. Replace cardboard with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) Observed employee personal gallon of milk being stored above bulk sugar used for product for customers. Ensure all employee personal food and drink are stored below all products served to customers. Smaller personal drinks should have a lid and a straw, stored on lowest level to prevent contamination. Reference 6-305.11.
